relevance_note: Case 4 describes a family in which a NOD2 variant segregates with arthritis: 'a heterozygous pathogenic variant in CARD15 (NOD2) (c.1001G>A; p.Arg334Gln) in all three affected individuals'.
method_note: Read by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and checked spans. Cases 1-3 (MAFB, PRG4 variants) are out of scope and get no rows; cohort_size_as_stated = 4 cases. In scope: Case 4 proband (labelled 'Case 4' from the section heading and Table 1 case number), his two sons (no own labels; 'son of Case 4', 'son of Case 4 2'), and the tested-negative 'unaffected mother of both sons' (labelled 'mother of son of Case 4'; no variant row, no feature rows because 'unaffected' names no specific feature). Also four previously published carriers of the same variant from ref [23], mentioned in the Case 4 discussion (labels 'ref [23] patient' to 'ref [23] patient 4' in order of mention: 1-2 = first family, 3-4 = second family; patient 3 is the one with skin lesions, patient 4 the one with camptodactyly, by order in the sentence). Their variant string is taken from the paper's own statement that it is the same variant as in the family; zygosity/pathogenicity left not reported for them. 'All key features of Blau syndrome' for ref [23] family 1 was recorded as a feature row only; checklist items left not reported because mapping to the triad needs a second sentence. 'Skin lesions' was not mapped to the checklist skin item (broader than rash/dermatitis). Table 1 case 4 rows: Granulomatous empty, Uveitis and Dermatitis 'Unknown' -> not reported; 'Typically raised' inflammatory markers describe the condition, not the patient, so not used. The text says uveitis, skin lesions and camptodactyly 'were not reported' for the family: treated as silence, not exclusion. Table 1 consanguinity 'No' applied to the proband only. Proband onset 'in childhood' taken from his presentation with arthritis; the JIA diagnosis in childhood is a misdiagnosis, so age at diagnosis left not reported; 'in adulthood' (recruitment) recorded as last evaluation. Sons' inheritance recorded as paternal: variant present in the affected father (proband) and absent in their mother; the paper does not use the word inherited. Sons' disease label is Blau syndrome from Table 1 case 4, though the text says they were diagnosed with JIA. Table 1 'Inheritance AD' is the mode of inheritance, not the variant origin, so proband inheritance is not reported. Gene printed as 'CARD15 (NOD2)'. cites_prior_report left null: the paper does not say its own patients were published before.
